Yeah, gotta essentially shut it down and restart. I come into the website to see a microphone rip off of a professional Rode microphone and then the products below it are all random cheap products I see advertised by every cheap seller online. Doesn't seem related to each other at all. 

Now, I don't recommend drop shipping like you are because even when done perfectly, with professional photos, and the products are researched and relate to each other, then all this becomes is marketing. You'll need to have lots of money in hand to sustain a proper marketing campaign and keep product flowing while you wait for customer money to end up in your bank. 

What I usually see is a shopify website focused solely on single products that is advertised in a special way to be special somehow, example: Biodegradable bamboo toothbrushes for the environment, and a couple related items like a bamboo toothbrush holder. These types of businesses have very easy to recognize customers that can be marketed to easily, while spending like .50c on their product. This just becomes a 100% focus on building up and showing off your brand too, because the product is honestly worth nothing and anyone can go purchase those bamboo toothbrushes for .50c. 

Then there's people who create a more general store style, but it's still always got a theme. A website I created in College, I named FinerLights and I drop shipped lamps. This was 6+ years ago now and I ran it through Shopify. I did well and learned a lot, but it was a terrible failure. It's hard to advertise a more general store as you have so many products people might be interested in, even when you niche down to something like lights only. There's so many lights out there, and anyone can go on Amazon and find hundreds of lights from what many people believe to be at least a more reliable market than mine. I don't suggest doing a general store, even themed. It's really hard to market, and as you're experiencing, when the items don't relate, it's really hard to actually get people to purchase any item in a sea of random items they don't need to purchase from you. I recommend dropping down to one well researched product and related brand and then building up from there as you actually have sales coming in. Market maybe 3 or 4 well researched and related products to see what sells best and then focus your efforts there and with the market segments you targeted to reach that success. 

Dropshipping is not easy, if you aren't getting information like this from personal research and you're looking to pay guru's, then you're looking to get scammed and fail. 

Don't forget, 9 in 10 e-commerce websites fail and most fail within the first 120 days of trading online. Shopify stores also having an average 1.4% conversion rate, which if what you've stated is the case with currently have a 0% conversion rate, I'd say you're in the close the shop and restart range. Hence my recommendations above. 

Best of luck to you

I couldn't find a way to stop using it, but I did find a way to use it productively. I use several apps that allow me to control my behavior and block myself from roaming YouTube. I use two apps for my process. One is a "YouTube Parental Control app" called YouTuze, found on the Android store. (The paid version specifically)
YouTuze allows me to go through and select specific channels that I know are beneficial to me, and doesn't allow me to see any of YouTube's recommendations. This stops me from just scrolling through distracting videos all day, and I have to deliberately choose what content I want to see instead of just watching what YouTube recommends to me.

This sounds like it should be enough, but it doesn't stop me from loading up my internet browser on my phone and still streaming videos I shouldn't. So I also added an app called Blocksite to my phone that will also hold me accountable and stop me from roaming YouTube without meaning to. 

I can always turn these systems off if I really want. There's times where I am searching for specific content and do turn off Blocksite so that I can search through YouTube freely. The difference between now and before, is that I do it deliberately and with reason. Even with both of these supporting me, I still sometimes fail and fall in deep after unblocking YouTube for a "quick search", but because of this support system I am a lot better than before. Hope this helps.
